name: Halliburton

summary.text: Halliburton Company is an oilfield services company headquartered in Houston. Dick Cheney was its chairman and chief executive officer from 1995 to 2000, between serving as Secretary of Defense and as Vice President. Its engineering and construction subsidiary Kellogg Brown & Root (KBR) held the Army's LOGCAP logistics support contract and, on March 8, 2003, received a no-bid Restore Iraqi Oil contract from the Army Corps of Engineers; a December 2004 House minority staff report put Halliburton's Iraq work at $8.3 billion under LOGCAP and $2.5 billion under RIO. Halliburton completed its separation from KBR on April 5, 2007. In February 2009 KBR LLC pleaded guilty to Foreign Corrupt Practices Act charges over bribes in Nigeria with a $402 million criminal penalty, of which Halliburton paid $382 million under its separation indemnity, and Halliburton and KBR jointly paid $177 million to settle SEC civil charges.

facts.claim: Dick Cheney served as chairman of the board and chief executive officer of Halliburton from 1995 to 2000, after a stint as a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (1993–1995) and before becoming Vice President in 2001; his office says he severed all ties with Halliburton and KBR in the summer of 2000.
facts.quote: That same year, he became chairman of the board and chief executive officer (CEO) of Halliburton Company.

sources.title: Whistleblower exposes $7 billion no-bid Defense Department contract

facts.claim: The Army's LOGCAP logistics contracts were awarded without open tender to a few U.S. firms, the largest being Halliburton and its subsidiary Kellogg, Brown & Root, on a cost-plus basis under which the contractor charges what it has spent and adds a profit.
facts.quote: They were awarded to a few US firms, the largest being Halliburton and its subsidiary Kellogg, Brown & Root.

sources.title: Where has all the money gone? On the Take in Iraq

facts.claim: On March 8, 2003, the Army Corps of Engineers awarded KBR the no-bid Restore Iraqi Oil (RIO) contract. A March 5, 2003 email by an Army Corps official described the award as having been "coordinated" with Vice President Cheney's office; Cheney's spokesman denied involvement.
facts.quote: a March 5, 2003, e-mail written by an Army Corps official referred to the awarding of the oil restoration contract as having been "coordinated" with Vice President Richard Cheney's office

sources.title: Documents reveal concern regarding Halliburton contracts

facts.claim: The Comptroller General later found that the oil infrastructure work was not within the scope of the overall LOGCAP contract.
facts.quote: the oil infrastructure work was not "within the scope of the overall LOGCAP contract."

sources.title: Documents reveal concern regarding Halliburton contracts

facts.claim: Bunnatine Greenhouse, the Army Corps of Engineers' chief contracting oversight official, objected publicly to the no-bid KBR contract, was demoted, and in 2011 reached a $970,000 settlement with the government.
facts.quote: the former chief oversight official of contracts at the Army Corps of Engineers has reached a $970,000 settlement six years after she was demoted

sources.title: Fired Army Whistleblower Receives $970K for Exposing Halliburton No-Bid Contract in Iraq
Whistleblower exposes $7 billion no-bid Defense Department contract

facts.claim: A December 2004 report by the House Committee on Government Reform minority staff under Rep. Henry Waxman put Halliburton's Iraq work at more than $10 billion: $8.3 billion under the LOGCAP troop-support contract and $2.5 billion under the no-bid RIO contract, and cited at least nine government audit reports criticizing the company's Iraq work.
facts.quote: $8.3 billion in Iraq work under its LOGCAP troop support contract and $2.5 billion under its no-bid Restore Iraqi Oil (RIO) contract

sources.publisher: U.S. House Committee on Government Reform, Minority Staff (Rep. Henry A. Waxman)

facts.claim: KBR completed an initial public offering of 32,016,000 shares in November 2006 for net proceeds of $511 million; on April 5, 2007 Halliburton exchanged its remaining 135,627,000 KBR shares, about 81% of KBR's outstanding stock, for 85,273,184 Halliburton shares tendered by its stockholders, completing the separation.
facts.quote: Halliburton exchanged the 135,627,000 shares of KBR common stock owned by Halliburton, representing approximately 81% of KBR's outstanding common stock, for 85,273,184 shares of Halliburton common stock tendered by Halliburton stockholders

facts.claim: In February 2009 KBR LLC pleaded guilty in federal court in Houston to one count of conspiring to violate the FCPA and four counts of violating it, arising from bribes to Nigerian officials paid through agents of the TSKJ joint venture on the Bonny Island project; the $402 million criminal penalty was split with Halliburton paying $382 million under the master separation agreement's indemnity and KBR $20 million, and KBR accepted three years of probation with a compliance monitor.
facts.quote: The plea called for a criminal penalty of $402 million. Halliburton would pay $382 million under the indemnity in the master separation agreement, while KBR would pay $20 million.

Halliburton agrees to pay $560 million in KBR bribery

facts.claim: To settle the SEC's civil complaint alleging violations of the FCPA's anti-bribery and books-and-records provisions over Bonny Island, Halliburton and KBR, jointly and severally, agreed to pay $177 million, all of which Halliburton paid under the separation indemnity; the Department of Justice resolved its investigation of Halliburton with a non-prosecution agreement.
facts.quote: Halliburton and KBR, jointly and severally, agreed to make payments totaling $177 million, all of which has been paid by Halliburton pursuant to the indemnification under the master separation agreement.

openQuestions: The site's $39.5 billion figure for KBR's Iraq-related contracts (Financial Times, 2013) was not re-sourced; the Waxman report's $10.8 billion covers only through late 2004.
Cheney's 1995–2000 tenure is sourced to a Fox News fact sheet; a Halliburton proxy statement or 10-K from the period would be a primary source.
The Comptroller General (GAO) finding on the RIO contract scope is quoted via ICIJ; the GAO decision itself was not located.
The SEC complaint PDF is cited for the civil settlement; the $177 million figure and its characterization come from the companies' 10-Q filings.
